country.name: Japan
country.kicker: An island nation with a global imagination.

overview.summary: A mountainous archipelago that became an industrial powerhouse. Japan combines dense, connected cities with a shrinking population, and turns meticulous craft into everything from cars to culture.
overview.geography: An island chain off the eastern edge of Asia. Mountains compress much of urban life into coastal plains; the Pacific is both a connection and a source of natural hazards.

whyItMatters.title: Things the world runs on
whyItMatters.text: Cars, precision machinery, and advanced materials make Japan central to global industry, far beyond its familiar consumer brands.

whyItMatters.title: A glimpse of an older future
whyItMatters.text: Its aging society is testing how work, care, and communities adapt when there are fewer young people.

stories.question: Why do so many people live along one coast?
stories.summary: Mountains and the sea leave a surprisingly narrow stage for everyday life.

sections.title: A country with little flat land
sections.text: Much of Japan is mountainous. Large cities grew on plains and around sheltered bays, where transport, housing, and industry can fit together.

sections.title: A connected urban belt
sections.text: Tokyo, Nagoya, and Osaka anchor the Pacific-side corridor. Rail links knit these dense regions together; other parts of Japan remain rural and sparsely populated.

stories.takeaway: Think of Japan as a chain of connected coastal regions, not one enormous city.

scene.mapNote: Notice the long Pacific coast and the narrow shape of the islands.

next.reason: Follow the region’s connected manufacturing systems.
A different path into the global economy.

stories.question: How did Japan become a manufacturing powerhouse?
stories.summary: The story is about learning, rebuilding, and improving systems.

sections.title: Two waves of transformation
sections.text: Industrialization accelerated in the late nineteenth century. After World War II, rebuilding, education, investment, and expanding world trade helped industry grow again.

sections.title: The less visible strengths
sections.text: A finished car is only part of the story. Specialist suppliers, production methods, components, and materials connect Japan to factories across the world.

stories.takeaway: Japan’s industrial influence is as much inside other products as on the labels you recognize.

scene.mapNote: Sea connections link Japanese factories to East Asian production networks.

next.reason: Follow the production networks across East Asia.
A different path into the global economy.

stories.question: What changes when a country grows older?
stories.summary: Japan offers an early view of a challenge many societies will face.

sections.title: Long lives, fewer births
sections.text: Low fertility and long life expectancy reshape the age balance. In October 2024, 29.3% of the population was 65 or older.

sections.title: Different places, different futures
sections.text: Aging raises demand for care and strains the labor supply. Some big cities still attract people while smaller communities contend with vacant homes and fewer services.

stories.takeaway: An older population changes where people live, how they work, and who looks after whom.

scene.mapNote: A long archipelago contains very different local population stories.
